title: Audiences in New York, Chicago, Texas and the South
summary: He compares how audiences received the band in different regions.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, how would you compare the musical environments as you travelled all over? Say, in New York, down South, in Chicago, out on the coast, you were just speaking of Texas. How did it differ? I mean, the social environment and the musical environment. Can you remember anything about that?

Well, New York, New York and Chicago. People received you about the same. It may be a little different in a way. But, if they like you, they'll show how they like you. They'd jump around. Chicago is a big
city for music, which you know. Texas. I played a lot of schools there and also one night stands. So, they received us very good. I played a lot of proms and all that.

All the places in the South, if people are going out for one-night stands, they start preparing for that night say weeks ahead of time. You know. Their dress and whatever they're gonna do cause it was just like going out to a show for them cause they don't get those name bands there too often. But when they come out, they have a lot of fun. They have tables and dance.
We didn't play too many theaters too far deep South because they didn't have too much Vaudeville there. Theatres good for that. (Inaudible).
Well, you get into New Orleans and you've got another big place that's used to a lot of jazz music. So, they was up for it.
